segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 مصطلحات اليوم

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **النتح** (Transpiration) — تبخر الماء من أوراق النبات عبر الثغور؛ التكلفة التي لا مفر منها لفتح المسام لامتصاص CO2.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **الثغور** (Stomata) — مسام مجهرية قابلة للتعديل على أسطح الأوراق تسمح بدخول CO2 وخروج بخار الماء؛ يغلقها النبات تحت الضغط.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **السعة الحقلية** (Field capacity) — الرطوبة التي تحتفظ بها التربة بعد أن قامت الجاذبية بتصريف المسام الكبيرة، تاركة الماء والهواء متاحين للجذور؛ الحالة المستهدفة.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **نقطة الذبول الدائم** (Permanent wilting point) — مستوى الرطوبة الذي يتم عنده الاحتفاظ بماء التربة المتبقي بقوة أكبر مما تستطيع الجذور استخلاصه، ولا يستطيع النبات التعافي.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **النتح التبخري** (Evapotranspiration - ET) — فقدان الماء المشترك من نتح النبات وتبخر سطح التربة؛ رقم "السحب" في جدولة الري.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **صرف البلاط** (Tile drainage) — أنابيب مثقبة مدفونة تحت منطقة الجذر لتصريف المياه الزائدة ومنع الجذور من الاختناق في التربة المشبعة.

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — C.
segments.tr: *الإجابات: 1 — ج.

segments.src: Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: أكثر من 99% من الماء الممتص يمر عبر النبات ويتبخر؛ جزء صغير فقط ينتهي كأنسجة نباتية.

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: هذه هي المقايضة التي يقوم بها النبات للحصول على CO2 لعملية التمثيل الضوئي.

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
segments.tr: 2 — خطأ.

segments.src: The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: الحالة الأكثر رطوبة هي التشبع، حيث تكون كل مسام ممتلئة بالماء ولا يوجد أكسجين للجذور.

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: السعة الحقلية هي ما يتبقى بعد أن تصرف الجاذبية المسام الكبيرة، وهي الحالة المرغوبة بدقة لأن الماء والهواء موجودان معًا.

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: يوصل الري بالتنقيط والري الدقيق الماء مباشرة عند قاعدة النبات ويصل عادة إلى كفاءة 85 إلى 95%، مقابل حوالي 40 إلى 60% للطرق السطحية.

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: المقايضة هي تكلفة التركيب العالية والحاجة إلى مياه نظيفة ومفلترة لتجنب انسداد البواعث.*

fr.title: [Agriculture 101 #5] Une plante de maïs boit comme un tuyau d'incendie — et n'en garde presque rien

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > Les cultures déplacent d'énormes quantités d'eau du sol vers l'air, et l'irrigation consiste essentiellement à empêcher ce pipeline de s'assécher — sans pour autant noyer les racines.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Concept du jour

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: Voici un fait qui surprend la plupart des gens : une plante utilise moins de 1 % de l'eau qu'elle absorbe pour se construire elle-même.

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: Les 99 % restants traversent directement la plante et s'évaporent par ses feuilles.

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: Ce processus est appelé **transpiration**, et ce n'est pas du gaspillage.

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: C'est le prix à payer pour se nourrir.

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: Les feuilles sont recouvertes de pores microscopiques ajustables appelés **stomates**.

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: Une plante doit les ouvrir pour laisser entrer le dioxyde de carbone — le CO2 est la matière première de la photosynthèse, la réaction de production de sucre qui devient grain, fruit et fibre.

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: Mais l'intérieur d'une feuille est une surface humide, et l'air extérieur est généralement plus sec.

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: Dès que ces pores s'ouvrent, la vapeur d'eau s'échappe.

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: Il n'y a aucun moyen d'inhaler du CO2 sans expirer de l'eau.

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: Les agriculteurs appellent parfois cela le « commerce carbone-contre-eau » de la plante.

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: La vapeur qui s'échappe tire un fil continu d'eau depuis les racines.

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: Les molécules d'eau s'accrochent les unes aux autres (cohésion) et aux parois de la tuyauterie étroite de la plante, le **xylème**.

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: Ainsi, l'évaporation au sommet tire littéralement la colonne vers le haut — pas de pompe, pas de cœur, juste de la tension.

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: Un grand plant de maïs par une chaude journée de juillet dans l'Iowa peut déplacer deux à quatre litres à travers cette paille.

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: La sécheresse de l'air détermine le taux de traction.

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: C'est le **déficit de pression de vapeur** (DPV) — l'écart entre la quantité d'humidité que l'air contient et celle qu'il pourrait contenir.

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: Les journées chaudes, sèches et venteuses signifient un grand déficit et une forte traction.

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: Les journées fraîches, humides et calmes signifient une traction douce.

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi le même champ peut avoir besoin du double d'eau lors d'une vague de chaleur.

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: Passons maintenant au côté sol.

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: L'eau dans le sol n'est pas un réservoir plein que l'on vide uniformément.

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: Trois points de repère sont importants :

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **Saturation** — chaque pore est rempli d'eau, et aucun n'est rempli d'air. Les racines ont aussi besoin d'oxygène, donc c'est un compte à rebours, pas un bon état.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **Capacité au champ** — la gravité a drainé les gros pores (généralement un jour ou deux après une pluie battante), l'eau reste dans les petits, et l'air est revenu. C'est l'état idéal.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **Point de flétrissement permanent** — l'eau restante s'accroche aux particules du sol plus fermement que les racines ne peuvent tirer. Il y a encore de l'eau là-bas ; la plante ne peut tout simplement pas l'atteindre.

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: La plage utilisable entre la capacité au champ et le point de flétrissement est l'**eau disponible pour la plante**.

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: Le sol sableux a de gros pores qui se drainent rapidement et retiennent peut-être un pouce d'eau par pied de profondeur.

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: Le limon limoneux en retient deux ou plus.

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: Ce chiffre unique explique pourquoi une colline de sable du Nebraska nécessite une irrigation légère fréquente alors qu'un limon limoneux de l'Illinois peut tenir une semaine.

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: Lorsque l'eau disponible devient faible, la plante atteint le **stress hydrique**.

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: Sa première défense est de fermer les stomates — ce qui arrête la perte d'eau mais arrête aussi l'absorption de CO2, donc la croissance s'interrompt.

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: Si cela continue, les feuilles s'enroulent, se flétrissent et tombent.

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: Le moment compte plus que le total : le stress pendant la floraison et la pollinisation coûte beaucoup plus cher en rendement que le même stress pendant la croissance végétative précoce.

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: Dans le maïs, quelques jours secs à l'apparition des soies peuvent réduire le rendement d'un tiers.

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: L'échec opposé est tout aussi réel.

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **L'engorgement** remplit chaque pore, les racines suffoquent, et dans un sol chaud, elles peuvent mourir en 48 à 72 heures.

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi le **drainage** — nivellement de surface, ou tuyau perforé enterré appelé **drainage par tuyaux** — est une forme de gestion de l'eau tout aussi importante que l'irrigation.

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: Une grande partie du Midwest américain n'est cultivable que parce qu'elle a été drainée.

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: Alors, comment acheminer l'eau ?

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: Trois grandes familles, dans l'ordre approximatif de leur efficacité :

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **Irrigation de surface (inondation/sillon)** — l'eau s'écoule dans le champ par gravité. Bon marché, ancienne, sans coût énergétique, mais généralement seulement 40 à 60 % de l'eau appliquée atteint la zone racinaire. Le reste s'écoule ou percole au-delà des racines.

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **Irrigation par aspersion** — sous pression, pulvérisée d'en haut. Le pivot central, ces cercles verts que vous voyez depuis un avion au-dessus du Kansas, est la forme dominante. Environ 70 à 90 % d'efficacité ; les buses à basse pression près du sol battent les canons à haute pression car moins de pulvérisation s'évapore en vol.

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **Goutte-à-goutte / micro-irrigation** — les émetteurs libèrent l'eau lentement juste à la base de chaque plante. 85 à 95 % d'efficacité, permet de délivrer de l'engrais dans l'eau (**fertirrigation**), et garde le feuillage sec, ce qui supprime certaines maladies. Le piège est le coût initial et les émetteurs bouchés si l'eau n'est pas filtrée.

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: Décider *quand* irriguer utilise l'une des deux logiques.

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **Basée sur le sol** : placez des capteurs dans le sol et arrosez lorsque l'humidité descend en dessous d'un seuil.

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **Basée sur la météo** : tenez un carnet de comptes.

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: Estimez la quantité d'eau qui a quitté le champ par **évapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration des plantes plus évaporation du sol), soustrayez la pluie, et remplissez le déficit.

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: En termes simples :

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: Les réseaux publics d'ET publient des chiffres quotidiens exactement à cette fin, et un coefficient de culture ajuste le chiffre de référence à ce que vous cultivez à n'importe quel stade de croissance.

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: Une autre idée qui vaut la peine d'être connue : **l'irrigation déficitaire**.

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: Parfois, sous-arroser délibérément pendant un stade où la culture est insensible permet d'économiser beaucoup d'eau pour une petite perte de rendement — et dans les vignes à vin, un stress léger améliore en fait la qualité du fruit en concentrant les sucres et les composés aromatiques.

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: Plus d'eau n'est pas toujours mieux.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dans la vie quotidienne

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: Prenez l'avion pour Denver ou Wichita par un après-midi clair et regardez en bas.

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: Le sol est une courtepointe de cercles verts parfaits, chacun d'environ un demi-mile de diamètre, emballés dans des champs carrés.

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: Ce sont des pivots centraux — un bras d'arroseurs d'un quart de mile tournant lentement autour d'un puits.

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: Les coins restent bruns parce que le bras ne peut pas les atteindre.

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: La plupart de ces puits puisent dans l'aquifère d'Ogallala, la vaste couche d'eau souterraine sous les Hautes Plaines.

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: C'est une leçon utile sur l'économie de l'irrigation.

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: Dans certaines parties de l'ouest du Kansas, la nappe phréatique a baissé de plus de 100 pieds depuis que le pompage à grande échelle a commencé, et pomper plus profondément coûte plus de diesel ou d'électricité chaque année.

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: Ce coût croissant est la raison pour laquelle les agriculteurs là-bas ont échangé les canons à haute pression contre des buses à basse pression, puis ont ajouté des sondes d'humidité du sol, et dans certains comtés ont volontairement accepté de pomper moins.

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: L'efficacité a cessé d'être un slogan environnemental pour devenir un poste budgétaire.

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: Pendant ce temps, dans la vallée centrale de Californie — qui cultive la plupart des amandes, pistaches et tomates de transformation aux États-Unis.

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: — l'histoire a pris une autre tournure.

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: Les cultures permanentes d'arbres et de vignes ne peuvent pas être mises en jachère lors d'une année sèche comme peut l'être une culture annuelle en rangs ; vous arrosez le verger ou vous perdez un investissement de 20 ans.

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: Cette pression a poussé la vallée fortement vers le goutte-à-goutte et les micro-asperseurs, et vers des lignes de goutte-à-goutte enterrées pour les tomates.

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: L'eau dans ce système se négocie sur un marché ouvert, parfois pour plusieurs centaines de dollars par acre-pied lors d'une année de sécheresse, ce qui rend chaque point de pourcentage d'efficacité rentable.

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: Vous pouvez observer la même physique dans votre propre jardin.

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: Arrosez une pelouse à 14h

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: en août et une part significative s'évapore avant d'atterrir.

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Arrosez à 5h du matin

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: et presque tout s'imprègne — même tuyau, mêmes minutes, plus d'eau dans la zone racinaire.

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: Et le conseil standard d'arroser profondément mais moins souvent est aussi de la physique du sol : une aspersion quotidienne légère ne mouille que le pouce supérieur, donc les racines restent superficielles et la plante devient fragile dès que vous sautez un jour.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Résumé en trois lignes

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. Les plantes doivent ouvrir leurs stomates pour absorber le CO2, donc la transpiration — perdre de l'eau dans l'air — est un coût inévitable de la photosynthèse, dicté par la sécheresse de l'air.

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. L'eau du sol utilisable se situe entre la capacité au champ et le point de flétrissement ; trop peu provoque un stress hydrique qui nuit le plus pendant la floraison, et trop étouffe les racines, c'est pourquoi le drainage compte autant que l'irrigation.

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. Les méthodes d'irrigation vont des systèmes d'inondation bon marché et fuyants au goutte-à-goutte précis et coûteux, et la planification se fait soit par des capteurs d'humidité du sol, soit par un carnet de comptes d'évapotranspiration qui suit l'eau entrante par rapport à l'eau sortante.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termes du jour

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **Transpiration** — Eau s'évaporant des feuilles d'une plante à travers les stomates ; le coût inévitable de l'ouverture des pores pour absorber le CO2.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **Stomates** — Pores microscopiques ajustables sur les surfaces des feuilles qui laissent entrer le CO2 et sortir la vapeur d'eau ; la plante les ferme en cas de stress.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **Capacité au champ** — L'humidité qu'un sol retient après que la gravité a drainé les gros pores, laissant à la fois de l'eau et de l'air disponibles pour les racines ; la condition cible.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **Point de flétrissement permanent** — Le niveau d'humidité auquel l'eau restante du sol est retenue trop fermement pour que les racines puissent l'extraire, et la plante ne peut pas récupérer.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **Évapotranspiration (ET)** — Perte d'eau combinée de la transpiration des plantes et de l'évaporation de la surface du sol ; le chiffre de « retrait » dans la planification de l'irrigation.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **Drainage par tuyaux** — Tuyau perforé enterré sous la zone racinaire pour évacuer l'excès d'eau et empêcher les racines de suffoquer dans un sol saturé.

pt.title: [Agricultura 101 #5] Uma planta de milho bebe como uma mangueira de incêndio — e quase não retém nada disso

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > As culturas movem quantidades enormes de água do solo para o ar, e a irrigação é, na verdade, apenas o trabalho de manter esse encanamento sem secar — sem afogar as raízes.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Conceito de hoje

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: Aqui está um fato que surpreende a maioria das pessoas: uma planta usa menos de 1% da água que absorve para realmente se construir.

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: Os outros 99% ou mais passam direto e evaporam de suas folhas.

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: Esse processo é chamado de **transpiração**, e não é desperdício.

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: É o preço de se alimentar.

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: As folhas são cobertas por poros microscópicos ajustáveis chamados **estômatos**.

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: Uma planta precisa abri-los para deixar o dióxido de carbono entrar — o CO2 é a matéria-prima para a fotossíntese, a reação de produção de açúcar que se torna grão, fruta e fibra.

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: Mas o interior de uma folha é uma superfície úmida, e o ar externo geralmente é mais seco.

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: No instante em que esses poros se abrem, o vapor de água sai rapidamente.

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: Não há como inalar CO2 sem exalar água.

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: Os agricultores às vezes chamam isso de "troca de carbono por água" da planta.

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: O vapor que escapa puxa um fio contínuo de água das raízes.

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: As moléculas de água se unem (coesão) e aderem às paredes do encanamento estreito da planta, o **xilema**.

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: Portanto, a evaporação no topo literalmente arrasta a coluna para cima — sem bomba, sem coração, apenas tensão.

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: Uma planta de milho alta em um dia quente de julho em Iowa pode mover de dois a quatro litros através desse canudo.

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: A secura do ar define a taxa de tração.

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: Isso é o **déficit de pressão de vapor** (DPV) — a diferença entre quanta umidade o ar está retendo e quanta ele poderia reter.

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: Dias quentes, secos e com vento significam um grande déficit e uma tração forte.

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: Dias frescos, úmidos e calmos significam uma tração suave.

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: É por isso que o mesmo campo pode precisar do dobro de água em uma onda de calor.

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: Agora, o lado do solo.

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: A água no solo não é um tanque cheio que você esvazia uniformemente.

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: Três marcos são importantes:

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **Saturação** — cada poro está cheio de água, e nenhum está cheio de ar. As raízes também precisam de oxigênio, então este é um relógio de contagem regressiva, não um bom estado.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **Capacidade de campo** — a gravidade drenou os poros grandes (geralmente um ou dois dias após uma chuva forte), a água permanece nos pequenos e o ar voltou. Este é o ideal.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **Ponto de murcha permanente** — a água restante adere às partículas do solo com mais força do que as raízes conseguem puxar. Ainda há água lá embaixo; a planta simplesmente não consegue obtê-la.

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: A faixa utilizável entre a capacidade de campo e o ponto de murcha é a **água disponível para a planta**.

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: O solo arenoso tem poros grandes que drenam rápido e retém talvez uma polegada por pé de profundidade.

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: O solo franco-siltoso retém duas ou mais.

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: Esse único número explica por que uma colina de areia em Nebraska precisa de irrigação leve frequente, enquanto um solo franco-siltoso em Illinois pode aguentar por uma semana.

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: Quando a água disponível fica baixa, a planta atinge o **estresse hídrico**.

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: Sua primeira defesa é fechar os estômatos — o que interrompe a perda de água, mas também interrompe a entrada de CO2, então o crescimento pausa.

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: Se forçar mais, as folhas enrolam, murcham e caem.

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: O momento importa mais do que o total: o estresse durante a floração e a polinização custa muito mais em rendimento do que o mesmo estresse durante o crescimento vegetativo inicial.

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: No milho, alguns dias secos na emissão de espigas podem reduzir o rendimento em um terço.

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: A falha oposta é igualmente real.

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **Encharcamento** preenche cada poro, as raízes sufocam e, em solo quente, podem morrer em 48 a 72 horas.

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: É por isso que a **drenagem** — nivelamento de superfície ou tubos perfurados enterrados chamados de **drenagem subterrânea** — é uma forma de gestão da água tão importante quanto a irrigação.

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: Grande parte do Meio-Oeste americano só é cultivável porque foi drenada.

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: Então, como entregamos água?

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: Três grandes famílias, em ordem aproximada de eficiência:

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **Irrigação de superfície (inundação/sulco)** — a água corre pelo campo por gravidade. Barata, antiga, sem custo de energia, mas normalmente apenas 40 a 60% da água aplicada atinge a zona radicular. O restante escoa ou percola além das raízes.

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **Irrigação por aspersão** — pressurizada, pulverizada de cima. O pivô central, aqueles círculos verdes que você vê de um avião sobre o Kansas, é a forma dominante. Aproximadamente 70 a 90% de eficiência; bicos de baixa pressão perto do solo superam os canhões de alta pressão porque menos spray evapora durante o voo.

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **Gotejamento / microirrigação** — emissores liberam água lentamente bem na base de cada planta. 85 a 95% de eficiência, permite que fertilizantes sejam entregues na água (**fertirrigação**) e mantém a folhagem seca, o que suprime algumas doenças. O problema é o custo inicial e os emissores entupidos se a água não for filtrada.

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: Decidir *quando* irrigar usa uma de duas lógicas.

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **Baseada no solo**: coloque sensores no solo e irrigue quando a umidade cair abaixo de um limite.

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **Baseada no clima**: faça um controle de caixa.

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: Estime quanta água saiu do campo como **evapotranspiração** (ET — transpiração das plantas mais evaporação do solo), subtraia a chuva e reponha o déficit.

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: Em termos simples:

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: Redes públicas de ET publicam números diários exatamente para esse fim, e um coeficiente de cultura ajusta o valor de referência para o que você está cultivando em qualquer estágio de crescimento.

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: Mais uma ideia que vale a pena conhecer: **irrigação deficitária**.

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: Às vezes, sub-irrigar deliberadamente durante um estágio em que a cultura é insensível economiza muita água com uma pequena perda de rendimento — e em uvas para vinho, o estresse leve realmente melhora a qualidade da fruta ao concentrar açúcares e compostos de sabor.

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: Mais água nem sempre é melhor.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Na vida cotidiana

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: Voe para Denver ou Wichita em uma tarde clara e olhe para baixo.

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: O solo é uma colcha de retalhos de círculos verdes perfeitos, cada um com cerca de meia milha de diâmetro, compactados dentro de campos quadrados.

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: Esses são pivôs centrais — um braço de aspersores de um quarto de milha girando lentamente em torno de um poço.

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: Os cantos permanecem marrons porque o braço não consegue alcançá-los.

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: A maioria desses poços explora o Aquífero Ogallala, a vasta camada de água subterrânea sob as Grandes Planícies.

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: É uma lição útil sobre a economia da irrigação.

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: Em partes do oeste do Kansas, o nível freático caiu mais de 100 pés desde que o bombeamento em larga escala começou, e bombear de mais profundo custa mais diesel ou eletricidade a cada ano.

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: Esse custo crescente é o motivo pelo qual os agricultores de lá trocaram canhões de alta pressão por bicos de baixa pressão, depois adicionaram sondas de umidade do solo e, em alguns condados, concordaram voluntariamente em bombear menos.

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: A eficiência deixou de ser um slogan ambiental e tornou-se um item de custo.

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: Enquanto isso, no Vale Central da Califórnia — que cultiva a maioria das amêndoas, pistaches e tomates processados nos EUA.

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: — a história foi o contrário.

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: Culturas permanentes de árvores e videiras não podem ser deixadas em pousio em um ano seco da maneira que uma cultura anual pode; ou você irriga o pomar ou perde um investimento de 20 anos.

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: Essa pressão empurrou o vale fortemente para o gotejamento e microaspersores, e para linhas de gotejamento enterradas em tomates.

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: A água nesse sistema é negociada em um mercado aberto, às vezes por várias centenas de dólares por acre-pé em um ano de seca, o que torna cada ponto percentual de eficiência valioso em dinheiro real.

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: Você pode observar a mesma física no seu próprio quintal.

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: Regue um gramado às 14h

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: em agosto e uma parte significativa evapora antes de tocar o solo.

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Regue às 5h da manhã

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: e quase tudo é absorvido — mesma mangueira, mesmos minutos, mais água na zona radicular.

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: E o conselho padrão de regar profundamente, mas com menos frequência, também é física do solo: uma aspersão diária leve molha apenas a polegada superior, então as raízes permanecem rasas e a planta torna-se frágil no momento em que você pula um dia.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Resumo em três linhas

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. As plantas devem abrir seus estômatos para absorver CO2, então a transpiração — perder água para o ar — é um custo inevitável da fotossíntese, impulsionado por quão seco está o ar.

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. A água do solo utilizável situa-se entre a capacidade de campo e o ponto de murcha; muito pouca causa estresse hídrico que prejudica mais durante a floração, e muita sufoca as raízes, razão pela qual a drenagem é tão importante quanto a irrigação.

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. Os métodos de irrigação variam de sistemas de inundação baratos e com vazamentos a gotejamento caro e preciso, e o agendamento é feito por sensores de umidade do solo ou por um controle de evapotranspiração que rastreia a água que entra versus a que sai.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Quiz

segments.tr: Aproximadamente qual parcela da água que uma cultura absorve é realmente incorporada ao próprio tecido da planta?**

segments.src: - A) About 50%
segments.tr: - A) Cerca de 50%

segments.src: - B) About 20%
segments.tr: - B) Cerca de 20%

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de hoje

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **Transpiração** — Água evaporando das folhas de uma planta através dos estômatos; o custo inevitável de abrir poros para absorver CO2.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **Estômatos** — Poros microscópicos ajustáveis nas superfícies das folhas que deixam o CO2 entrar e o vapor de água sair; a planta os fecha sob estresse.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **Capacidade de campo** — A umidade que um solo retém após a gravidade ter drenado os poros grandes, deixando água e ar disponíveis para as raízes; a condição alvo.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **Ponto de murcha permanente** — O nível de umidade no qual a água restante no solo é retida com muita força para que as raízes possam extrair, e a planta não consegue se recuperar.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **Evapotranspiração (ET)** — Perda combinada de água da transpiração da planta e evaporação da superfície do solo; o número de "retirada" no agendamento de irrigação.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **Drenagem subterrânea** — Tubo perfurado enterrado abaixo da zona radicular para remover o excesso de água e evitar que as raízes sufoquem em solo saturado.

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — C.
segments.tr: *Respostas: 1 — C.

segments.src: Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: Bem mais de 99% da água absorvida passa direto e transpira; apenas uma pequena fração acaba como tecido vegetal.

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: Essa é a troca que uma planta faz para obter CO2 para a fotossíntese.

segments.src: The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: O estado mais úmido é a saturação, onde cada poro está cheio de água e as raízes não têm oxigênio.

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: A capacidade de campo é o que resta após a gravidade drenar os poros grandes, e é a condição desejável justamente porque água e ar estão presentes.

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: O gotejamento e a microirrigação entregam água diretamente na base da planta e normalmente atingem 85 a 95% de eficiência, contra cerca de 40 a 60% para métodos de superfície.

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: A compensação é o alto custo de instalação e a necessidade de água limpa e filtrada para evitar emissores entupidos.*

in.title: [Pertanian 101 #5] Tanaman Jagung Minum Seperti Selang Pemadam Kebakaran — Dan Hampir Tidak Menyimpan Apa Pun

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > Tanaman memindahkan sejumlah besar air dari tanah ke udara, dan irigasi pada dasarnya adalah tugas menjaga agar pipa tersebut tidak kering — tanpa membuat akarnya tenggelam.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Konsep Hari Ini

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: Berikut adalah fakta yang mengejutkan kebanyakan orang: tanaman menggunakan kurang dari 1% air yang diserapnya untuk benar-benar membangun dirinya sendiri.

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: Lebih dari 99% sisanya mengalir langsung dan menguap dari daunnya.

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: Proses itu disebut **transpirasi**, dan itu bukan pemborosan.

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: Itu adalah harga untuk makan.

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: Daun ditutupi oleh pori-pori mikroskopis yang dapat disesuaikan yang disebut **stomata**.

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: Tanaman harus membukanya untuk membiarkan karbon dioksida masuk — CO2 adalah bahan baku untuk fotosintesis, reaksi pembuatan gula yang menjadi biji-bijian, buah, dan serat.

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: Tetapi bagian dalam daun adalah permukaan yang basah, dan udara di luar biasanya lebih kering.

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: Saat pori-pori tersebut terbuka, uap air keluar dengan deras.

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: Tidak ada cara untuk menghirup CO2 tanpa mengembuskan air.

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: Petani terkadang menyebut ini sebagai "perdagangan karbon-untuk-air" tanaman.

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: Uap yang keluar menarik aliran air terus menerus dari akar.

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: Molekul air saling menempel (kohesi) dan menempel pada dinding pipa sempit tanaman, yaitu **xilem**.

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: Jadi penguapan di bagian atas benar-benar menyeret kolom ke atas — tanpa pompa, tanpa jantung, hanya ketegangan.

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: Tanaman jagung tinggi pada hari Juli yang panas di Iowa dapat memindahkan dua hingga empat liter melalui sedotan ini.

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: Kekeringan udara menentukan tingkat tarikan.

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: Itu adalah **defisit tekanan uap** (VPD) — kesenjangan antara seberapa banyak kelembapan yang ditahan udara dan seberapa banyak yang dapat ditahannya.

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: Hari yang panas, kering, dan berangin berarti defisit besar dan tarikan yang kuat.

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: Hari yang sejuk, lembap, dan tenang berarti tarikan yang lembut.

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: Inilah sebabnya mengapa ladang yang sama bisa membutuhkan air dua kali lipat dalam gelombang panas.

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: Sekarang sisi tanah.

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: Air di tanah bukanlah tangki penuh yang Anda kuras secara merata.

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: Tiga tonggak penting:

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **Saturasi** — setiap pori penuh dengan air, dan tidak ada yang penuh dengan udara. Akar juga butuh oksigen, jadi ini adalah jam hitung mundur, bukan kondisi yang baik.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **Kapasitas lapangan** — gravitasi telah menguras pori-pori besar (biasanya sehari atau dua hari setelah hujan deras), air tetap berada di pori-pori kecil, dan udara kembali. Ini adalah kondisi ideal.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **Titik layu permanen** — sisa air menempel pada partikel tanah lebih kuat daripada yang dapat ditarik oleh akar. Masih ada air di sana; tanaman tidak bisa mendapatkannya.

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: Kisaran yang dapat digunakan antara kapasitas lapangan dan titik layu adalah **air yang tersedia bagi tanaman**.

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: Tanah berpasir memiliki pori-pori besar yang cepat mengering dan menahan mungkin satu inci air per kaki kedalaman.

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: Lempung berdebu menahan dua atau lebih.

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: Angka tunggal itu menjelaskan mengapa bukit pasir Nebraska membutuhkan irigasi ringan yang sering sementara lempung berdebu Illinois dapat bertahan selama seminggu.

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: Ketika air yang tersedia menipis, tanaman mengalami **cekaman air**.

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: Pertahanan pertamanya adalah menutup stomata — yang menghentikan kehilangan air tetapi juga menghentikan penyerapan CO2, sehingga pertumbuhan berhenti.

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: Dorong lebih jauh dan daun akan menggulung, layu, dan gugur.

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: Waktu lebih penting daripada jumlah total: cekaman selama pembungaan dan penyerbukan jauh lebih mengorbankan hasil daripada cekaman yang sama selama pertumbuhan vegetatif awal.

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: Pada jagung, beberapa hari kering saat kemunculan rambut tongkol dapat mengurangi hasil sepertiganya.

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: Kegagalan sebaliknya sama nyatanya.

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **Penyiraman berlebih** mengisi setiap pori, akar mati lemas, dan di tanah yang hangat mereka dapat mati dalam waktu 48 hingga 72 jam.

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: Inilah sebabnya mengapa **drainase** — perataan permukaan, atau pipa berlubang yang dikubur yang disebut **drainase ubin** — adalah bentuk pengelolaan air yang sama pentingnya dengan irigasi.

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar Midwest Amerika dapat ditanami hanya karena telah dipasangi ubin drainase.

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: Lalu bagaimana cara kita mengalirkan air?

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: Tiga kelompok besar, dalam urutan efisiensi kasar:

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **Irigasi permukaan (banjir/alur)** — air mengalir menuruni ladang secara gravitasi. Murah, kuno, tanpa biaya energi, tetapi biasanya hanya 40 hingga 60% dari air yang diberikan mencapai zona akar. Sisanya mengalir begitu saja atau meresap melewati akar.

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **Irigasi tabur (sprinkler)** — bertekanan, disemprotkan dari atas. Poros tengah (center pivot), lingkaran hijau yang Anda lihat dari pesawat di atas Kansas, adalah bentuk yang dominan. Sekitar 70 hingga 90% efisien; nosel penurunan tekanan rendah di dekat tanah mengungguli meriam tekanan tinggi karena lebih sedikit semprotan yang menguap di udara.

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **Irigasi tetes / mikro** — emitor melepaskan air secara perlahan tepat di pangkal setiap tanaman. 85 hingga 95% efisien, memungkinkan pupuk disalurkan bersama air (**fertigasi**), dan menjaga dedaunan tetap kering, yang menekan beberapa penyakit. Kendalanya adalah biaya di muka dan emitor yang tersumbat jika air tidak disaring.

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: Memutuskan *kapan* harus mengirigasi menggunakan salah satu dari dua logika.

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **Berbasis tanah**: letakkan sensor di dalam tanah dan beri air ketika kelembapan turun melewati ambang batas.

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **Berbasis cuaca**: jalankan pembukuan.

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: Perkirakan berapa banyak air yang meninggalkan ladang sebagai **evapotranspirasi** (ET — transpirasi dari tanaman ditambah penguapan dari tanah), kurangi hujan, dan isi ulang defisitnya.

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: Dalam istilah sederhana:

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: Jaringan ET publik menerbitkan angka harian untuk tujuan ini, dan koefisien tanaman menskalakan angka referensi ke apa pun yang Anda tanam pada tahap pertumbuhan apa pun.

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: Satu gagasan lagi yang perlu diketahui: **irigasi defisit**.

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: Terkadang sengaja kekurangan air selama tahap di mana tanaman tidak peka menghemat banyak air untuk penurunan hasil yang kecil — dan pada buah anggur, cekaman ringan justru meningkatkan kualitas buah dengan memekatkan gula dan senyawa rasa.

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: Lebih banyak air tidak selalu lebih baik.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Dalam Kehidupan Sehari-hari

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: Terbanglah ke Denver atau Wichita pada sore hari yang cerah dan lihat ke bawah.

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: Tanahnya seperti selimut lingkaran hijau sempurna, masing-masing lebarnya sekitar setengah mil, dikemas di dalam ladang persegi.

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: Itu adalah poros tengah — lengan alat penyiram sepanjang seperempat mil yang berputar perlahan mengelilingi sumur.

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: Sudut-sudutnya tetap berwarna cokelat karena lengan tersebut tidak dapat menjangkaunya.

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: Sebagian besar sumur tersebut menyadap Akuifer Ogallala, lapisan air tanah yang luas di bawah Dataran Tinggi.

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: Itu adalah pelajaran yang berguna dalam bidang ekonomi irigasi.

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: Di beberapa bagian Kansas barat, permukaan air telah turun lebih dari 100 kaki sejak pemompaan skala besar dimulai, dan memompa dari tempat yang lebih dalam membutuhkan lebih banyak solar atau listrik setiap tahunnya.

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: Meningkatnya biaya itulah sebabnya petani di sana menukar meriam bertekanan tinggi dengan nosel tetes rendah, kemudian menambahkan probe kelembapan tanah, dan di beberapa wilayah secara sukarela setuju untuk memompa lebih sedikit.

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: Efisiensi berhenti menjadi slogan lingkungan dan menjadi pos anggaran.

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: Sementara itu di Lembah Tengah California — yang menanam sebagian besar almond, pistachio, dan tomat olahan di AS.

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: — ceritanya berjalan sebaliknya.

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: Tanaman pohon dan merambat permanen tidak dapat dibiarkan fuso (tidak ditanami) pada tahun kering seperti halnya tanaman semusim; Anda harus mengairi kebun atau kehilangan investasi 20 tahun.

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: Tekanan itu mendorong lembah tersebut secara besar-besaran ke arah tetes dan mikro-sprinkler, serta ke arah saluran tetes terkubur pada tomat.

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: Air dalam sistem itu diperdagangkan di pasar terbuka, terkadang seharga beberapa ratus dolar per kaki-akru pada tahun kekeringan, yang membuat setiap persentase efisiensi bernilai uang sungguhan.

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: Anda dapat melihat fisika yang sama di halaman Anda sendiri.

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: Sirami rumput pada pukul 2 siang.

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: pada bulan Agustus dan sebagian besar air menguap sebelum mendarat.

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Sirami pada pukul 5 pagi.

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: dan hampir semuanya meresap — selang yang sama, menit yang sama, lebih banyak air di zona akar.

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: Dan saran standar untuk menyiram secara mendalam tetapi lebih jarang juga merupakan fisika tanah: taburan ringan harian hanya membasahi satu inci teratas, sehingga akar tetap dangkal dan tanaman menjadi rapuh saat Anda melewatkan satu hari.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Ringkasan Tiga Baris

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. Tanaman harus membuka stomata mereka untuk menyerap CO2, sehingga transpirasi — kehilangan air ke udara — adalah biaya fotosintesis yang tidak dapat dihindari, yang didorong oleh seberapa kering udara.

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. Air tanah yang dapat digunakan berada di antara kapasitas lapangan dan titik layu; terlalu sedikit menyebabkan cekaman air yang paling merusak selama pembungaan, dan terlalu sedikit mencekik akar, itulah sebabnya drainase sama pentingnya dengan irigasi.

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. Metode irigasi berkisar dari sistem banjir yang murah dan bocor hingga tetes yang mahal dan tepat, dan penjadwalan dilakukan baik oleh sensor kelembapan tanah atau oleh pembukuan evapotranspirasi yang melacak air masuk versus air keluar.

segments.tr: ## ✅ Kuis Mandiri

segments.tr: - A) Sekitar 50%

segments.tr: - B) Sekitar 20%

segments.tr: - C) Kurang dari 1%

segments.src: - D) About 90%
segments.tr: - D) Sekitar 90%

segments.tr: B/S: Tanah pada "kapasitas lapangan" adalah kondisi basah maksimum, dengan setiap ruang pori terisi air.**

segments.src: Which irrigation method is generally the most efficient at delivering water to the root zone?**

segments.src: - A) Furrow (surface) irrigation
segments.tr: - A) Irigasi alur (permukaan)

segments.src: - B) High-pressure sprinkler guns

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Istilah Hari Ini

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **Transpirasi** — Air yang menguap dari daun tanaman melalui stomata; biaya yang tidak dapat dihindari dari membuka pori-pori untuk menyerap CO2.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **Stomata** — Pori-pori mikroskopis yang dapat disesuaikan pada permukaan daun yang membiarkan CO2 masuk dan uap air keluar; tanaman menutupnya dalam kondisi tertekan.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **Kapasitas lapangan** — Kelembapan yang ditahan tanah setelah gravitasi menguras pori-pori besar, menyisakan air dan udara yang tersedia bagi akar; kondisi target.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **Titik layu permanen** — Tingkat kelembapan di mana sisa air tanah ditahan terlalu kuat untuk diekstrak oleh akar, dan tanaman tidak dapat pulih.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **Evapotranspirasi (ET)** — Kehilangan air gabungan dari transpirasi tanaman dan penguapan permukaan tanah; angka "penarikan" dalam penjadwalan irigasi.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **Drainase ubin** — Pipa berlubang yang dikubur di bawah zona akar untuk membawa kelebihan air dan mencegah akar mati lemas di tanah jenuh.
