segments.tr: *Jawaban: 1 — C.

segments.src: Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: Lebih dari 99% air yang diserap melewati dan bertranspirasi jauh; hanya sebagian kecil yang berakhir sebagai jaringan tanaman.

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: Itulah perdagangan yang dilakukan tanaman untuk mendapatkan CO2 untuk fotosintesis.

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
segments.tr: 2 — S (Salah).

segments.src: The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: Kondisi terbasah adalah saturasi, di mana setiap pori terisi air dan akar tidak memiliki oksigen.

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: Kapasitas lapangan adalah apa yang tersisa setelah gravitasi menguras pori-pori besar, dan itu adalah kondisi yang diinginkan justru karena air dan udara keduanya ada.

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: Irigasi tetes dan mikro menyalurkan air langsung di pangkal tanaman dan biasanya mencapai efisiensi 85 hingga 95%, versus sekitar 40 hingga 60% untuk metode permukaan.

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: Korbannya adalah biaya pemasangan yang tinggi dan kebutuhan akan air bersih yang disaring untuk menghindari emitor yang tersumbat.*

ja.title: [農業入門 #5] トウモロコシは消防ホースのように水を飲み、そのほとんどを消費しない

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > 作物は土壌から空気中へ膨大な量の水を移動させており、灌漑とは、根を溺れさせることなく、そのパイプラインが干からびないように保つ作業にほかならない。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 本日のコンセプト

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: ほとんどの人が驚く事実がある。植物は吸収した水のうち、実際に自身の体を構築するのに使うのは1%未満である。

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: 残りの99%以上はそのまま通り抜け、葉から蒸発していく。

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: このプロセスは**蒸散（transpiration）**と呼ばれ、無駄ではない。

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: 食べるための代償である。

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: 葉は**気孔（stomata）**と呼ばれる顕微鏡サイズの調整可能な気孔に覆われている。

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: 植物は二酸化炭素を取り込むためにこれらを開かなければならない。CO2は、穀物、果物、繊維となる糖を作る反応である光合成の原材料である。

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: しかし、葉の内側は濡れた表面であり、外側の空気は通常より乾燥している。

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: それらの気孔が開いた瞬間、水蒸気が勢いよく外へ逃げ出す。

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: 水を吐き出さずにCO2を吸い込む方法はない。

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: 農家はこれを「水と炭素のトレードオフ」と呼ぶことがある。

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: 逃げる水蒸気は、根から連続した水の糸を引き上げる。

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: 水分子は互いに引き合い（凝集力）、植物の細い配管である**木部（xylem）**の壁にしがみつく。

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: そのため、上部での蒸発文字通り列を上向きに引っ張る。ポンプもなく、心臓もなく、ただ張力だけがある。

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: アイオワ州の暑い7い日の背の高いトウモロコシは、このストローを通って2〜4リットルの水を移動させることができる。

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: 空気の乾燥度が引き上げ速度を決める。

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: それが**蒸気圧差（VPD: vapor pressure deficit）**である。空気保持している水分量と保持できる水分量のギャップである。

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: 暑く、乾燥し、風の強い日は大きな赤字と強い引きを意味する。

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: 涼しく、湿度が高く、風のない日は穏やかな引きを意味する。

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: これが、同じ畑であっても熱波の中では2倍の水を必要とする理由である。

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: 次に土壌側について見ていこう。

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: 土壌中の水は、均等に引き下げるフルタンクではない。

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: 3つの重要な基準がある:

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **飽和（Saturation）** — すべての気孔が水で満たされ、空気で満たされているものはない。根も酸素を必要とするため、これは良い状態ではなくカウントダウンクロックである。

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **圃場容水量（Field capacity）** — 重力により大きな気孔が排水され（通常はたっぷりの雨の1日か2日後）、小さな気孔に水が残り、空気が戻る。これが理想的な状態である。

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **永久萎凋点（Permanent wilting point）** — 残った水が土壌粒子にしがみつき、根が引き抜くよりも強く保持される。下にはまだ水があるが、植物がそれを手に入れられない状態である。

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: 圃場容水量と萎凋点の間の利用可能な範囲が**土壌水分有効水分（plant-available water）**である。

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: 砂質土壌は水が早く抜ける大きな気孔を持ち、深さ1フィートあたり1インチほどの水を保持する。

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: シルトロームは2つ以上保持する。

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: この単一の数値が、ネブラスカの砂丘では頻繁な軽い灌漑が必要である一方、イリノイのシルトロームは1週間持ちこたえられる理由を説明している。

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: 利用可能な水が少なくなると、植物は**水分ストレス（water stress）**に陥る。

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: 最初の防御策は気孔を閉じることである。これにより水の損失は止まるが、CO2の取り込みも止まるため、成長が一時停止する。

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: さらに進むと、葉が丸まり、萎れ、落ちる。

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: 合計よりもタイミングが重要である。開花期や受粉期のストレスは、初期の栄養成長期の同じストレスよりもはるかに多くの収量を犠牲にする。

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: トウモロコシでは、絹糸抽出期の数日間の乾燥が収量を3分の1に減少させることがある。

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: 反対の失敗も同様に現実のものである。

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **滞水（Waterlogging）**はすべての気孔を満たし、根は窒息し、暖かい土壌では48〜72時間で死ぬ可能性がある。

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: これが、表面勾配や**暗渠排水（tile drainage）**と呼ばれる埋設された有孔管などの**排水（drainage）**が、灌漑と同じくらい重要な水管理の形である理由である。

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: アメリカ中西部の大部分は、タイル排水が設置されたからこそ耕作可能なのである。

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: それでは、どのように水を供給するのだろうか？

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: 効率のおおまかな順に3つの大きなグループがある:

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **表面灌漑（flood/furrow irrigation）** — 重力によって水が畑を流れ下る。安価で古く、エネルギーコストはかからないが、通常、適用された水の40〜60%しか根圏に届かない。残りは流出するか、根を通り越して浸透する。

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **スプリンクラー灌漑（Sprinkler irrigation）** — 加圧され、上から噴霧される。カンザス州の上空から飛行機で見える緑色の円であるセンターピボットが主流の形態である。約70〜90%効率的であり、地表近くの低圧ドロップノズルは、飛行中に蒸発するスプレーが少ないため、高圧ガンよりも優れている。

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **ドリップ・微量灌漑（Drip / micro-irrigation）** — エミッターが各植物の根元でゆっくりと水を放出する。85〜95%効率的であり、水中で肥料を供給でき（**施肥灌漑（fertigation）**）、葉を乾燥した状態に保つためいくつかの病気を抑制する。難点は初期費用と、水が濾過されていない場合のエミッターの目詰まりである。

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: いつ灌漑するかを決めるには、2つの論理のいずれかを使用する。

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **土壌ベース**: 地中にセンサーを設置し、湿度が閾値を超えて低下したときに水をやる。

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **気象ベース**: 家計簿をつけるように計算する。

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: **蒸発散量（ET — evapotranspiration: 植物からの蒸散と土壌からの蒸発の合計）**として畑からどれだけの水が失われたかを推定し、雨を差し引き、不足分を補充する。

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: 分かりやすく言うと:

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: 公開されているETネットワークはまさにこの目的のために毎日の数値を公開しており、作物係数が基準数値を何を生育段階であれ栽培しているものに合わせて調整する。

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: 知っておく価値のあるもう1つのアイデア：**不足灌漑（deficit irrigation）**。

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: 作物が敏感ではない段階で意図的に水やりを少なくすると、少量の収量のヒットと引き換えに多くの水を節約できる。ワイン用ブドウでは、軽度のストレスが糖分と香味成分を濃縮することで実際に果実の品質を向上させる。

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: 水が多ければ多いほど良いとは限らない。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活において

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: 晴れた日の午後にデンバーやウィチタへ飛行機で降り立ち、下を見下ろす。

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: 地面は完璧な緑色の円のキルトであり、それぞれが約半マイルの直径を持ち、正方形の畑の中に詰め込まれている。

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: あれらはセンターピボットである。井戸の周りをゆっくりと回転する4分の1マイルのスプリンクラーのアームである。

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: アームが届かないため、コーナーは茶色のまま残る。

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: それらの井戸のほとんどは、ハイプレーンズの下にある広大な地下水層であるオガララ帯水層を利用している。

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: これは灌漑の経済学についての良い教訓である。

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: 西カンザスの一部では、大規模な揚水が始まって以来、地下水位が100フィート以上低下しており、より深い場所からの揚水には毎年多くのディーゼルや電力がかかる。

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: そのコストの上昇こそが、そこの農家がハイプレンジガンを低ドロップノズルに交換し、土壌水分プローブを追加し、一部の郡では自主的に揚水を減らすことに同意した理由である。

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: 効率性は環境のスローガンではなくなり、経費項目となった。

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: 一方、米国のアーモンド、ピスタチオ、加工用トマトの大部分を栽培しているカリフォルニア州セントラルバレーでは

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: 話は逆の方向に向かった。

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: 永年性の樹木やツルの作物は、一年生の列状作物のように乾燥した年に休耕することはできない。果樹園に水をやるか、20年の投資を失うかのどちらかである。

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: そのプレッシャーにより、バレーはドリップやマイクロ・スプリンクラー、そしてトマトの埋設型ドリップラインへと大きく向かった。

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: そのシステムの水はオープン市場で取引されており、干ばつの年にはアーカーフットあたり数百ドルになることもあり、効率のすべてのパーセンテージポイントが実質的な価値を持つ。

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: 自分の庭でも同じ物理現象を見ることができる。

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: 8月の午後2時に芝生に水をやる。

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: と、着地する前にかなりの割合が蒸発してしまう。

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: 午前5時に水をやる。

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: すると、ほぼすべてが染み込む。同じホース、同じ時間で、根圏により多くの水が入る。

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: そして、深く、しかしより少なく水やりをするという標準的なアドバイスも土壌物理学に基づいている。軽い毎日のスプリンクラーは上部1インチしか濡らさないため、根は浅いままになり、1日サボった瞬間に植物はもろくなる。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## 3行まとめ

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. 植物はCO2を取り込むために気孔を開かなければならないため、水が空気中に失われる蒸散は、空気の乾燥度によって駆動される光合成の避けられない代償である。

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. 利用可能な土壌水分は圃場容水量と萎凋点の間に存在する。少なすぎると開花期に最も害を及ぼす水分ストレスを引き起こし、多すぎると根を窒息させる。これが灌漑と同じくらい排水が重要である理由である。

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. 灌漑方法は安価で漏れやすい洪水システムから高価で精密なドリップまでさまざまであり、スケジュール管理は土壌水分センサー、または水の出入りを追跡する蒸発散量の家計簿によって行われる。

segments.tr: ## ✅ セルフクイズ

segments.tr: 作物が吸収する水のうち、実際に植物自体の組織に組み込まれる割合はおおよそどれくらいか？**

segments.src: - A) About 50%
- B) About 20%
- C) Less than 1%

segments.src: - D) About 90%

segments.tr: O/X: 「圃場容水量」の土壌は可能な限り最も濡れた状態で、すべての気孔スペースが水で満たされている。**

segments.tr: 根圏に水を届ける上で、一般的に最も効率的な灌漑方法はどれか？**

segments.src: - A) Furrow (surface) irrigation

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 本日の用語

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **蒸散（Transpiration）** — 気孔を通って植物の葉から蒸発する水。CO2を吸収するために気孔を開くことの避けられない代償。

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **気孔（Stomata）** — CO2を取り込み水蒸気を逃がす、葉の表面にある調整可能な顕微鏡サイズの気孔。ストレス下で植物はこれらを閉じる。

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **圃場容水量（Field capacity）** — 重力が大きな気孔の水を排水した後に土壌が保持する水分で、水と空気の両方が根に利用可能な状態。目標とする条件。

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **永久萎凋点（Permanent wilting point）** — 残った土壌の水が根が抽出するにはあまりにも強く保持され、植物が回復できない水分レベル。

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **蒸発散量（Evapotranspiration: ET）** — 植物の蒸散と土壌表面の蒸発による複合的な水の損失。灌漑スケジューリングにおける「引き出し」の数値。

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **暗渠排水（Tile drainage）** — 余分な水を運び去り、飽和した土壌で根が窒息するのを防ぐために根圏の下に埋設された有孔管。

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — C.
Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: 吸収された水の99%以上が通過して蒸散し、ほんのごく一部だけが植物組織になる。

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: それが光合成のためにCO2を得るために植物が行うトレードオフである。

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: 最も濡れた状態は飽和であり、すべての気孔が水で満たされ、根には酸素がない。

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: 圃場容水量は重力が大きな気孔を排水した後に残るものであり、水と空気の両方が存在するため正確に望ましい条件である。

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: ドリップおよび微量灌漑は植物の根元に直接水を供給し、通常85〜95%の効率に達するが、表面方法では約40〜60%である。

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: トレードオフは、高い設置コストと、目詰まりしたエミッターを避けるための清潔でフィルターされた水の必要性である。*

de.title: [Landwirtschaft 101 #5] Eine Maispflanze trinkt wie ein Feuerwehrschlauch – und behält fast nichts davon

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > Pflanzen transportieren enorme Wassermengen vom Boden in die Luft, und Bewässerung besteht im Grunde nur darin, diese Leitung vor dem Austrocknen zu bewahren – ohne die Wurzeln zu ersticken.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Heutiges Konzept

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: Hier ist eine Tatsache, die die meisten Menschen überrascht: Eine Pflanze nutzt weniger als 1 % des Wassers, das sie aufnimmt, um sich tatsächlich selbst aufzubauen.

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: Die übrigen gut 99 % wandern direkt hindurch und verdunsten aus ihren Blättern.

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: Dieser Prozess nennt sich **Transpiration** und ist keine Verschwendung.

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: Er ist der Preis fürs Essen.

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: Blätter sind mit mikroskopisch kleinen, regulierbaren Poren überzogen, die **Stomata** (Spaltöffnungen) genannt werden.

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: Eine Pflanze muss sie öffnen, um Kohlendioxid hineinzulassen – CO2 ist der Rohstoff für die Photosynthese, die zuckerbildende Reaktion, aus der Getreide, Früchte und Fasern werden.

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: Aber das Innere eines Blattes ist eine feuchte Oberfläche, und die Luft draußen ist normalerweise trockenere.

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: In dem Moment, in dem sich diese Poren öffnen, schießt Wasserdampf heraus.

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: Es gibt keine Möglichkeit, CO2 einzuatmen, ohne Wasser auszuatmen.

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: Landwirte nennen dies manchmal den „Kohlenstoff-Wasser-Handel“ der Pflanze.

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: Der entweichende Dampf zieht einen kontinuierlichen Wasserfaden von den Wurzeln nach oben.

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: Wassermoleküle haften aneinander (Kohäsion) und an den Wänden der engen Leitungsbahnen der Pflanze, dem **Xylem**.

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: Die Verdunstung an der Spitze zieht die Säule also buchstäblich nach oben – keine Pumpe, kein Herz, nur Spannung.

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: Eine hohe Maispflanze an einem heißen Julitag in Iowa kann zwei bis vier Liter durch diesen Strohhalm bewegen.

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: Die Trockenheit der Luft bestimmt die Zugrate.

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: Das ist das **Sättigungsdefizit** (VPD) – die Lücke zwischen der Feuchtigkeit, die die Luft hält, und der, die sie halten könnte.

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: Heiße, trockene, windige Tage bedeuten ein großes Defizit und einen starken Zug.

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: Kühle, feuchte, windstille Tage bedeuten einen sanften.

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund kann dasselbe Feld in einer Hitzewelle die doppelte Menge Wasser benötigen.

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: Nun zur Bodenseite.

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: Wasser im Boden ist kein voller Tank, den man gleichmäßig leersaugt.

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: Drei Markierungspunkte sind wichtig:

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **Sättigung** – jede Pore ist voller Wasser und keine voller Luft. Wurzeln brauchen ebenfalls Sauerstoff, daher ist dies ein Countdown-Timer, kein guter Zustand.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **Feldkapazität** – die Schwerkraft hat die großen Poren entleert (normalerweise ein oder zwei Tage nach einem ergiebigen Regen), Wasser verbleibt in den kleinen und Luft ist zurück. Das ist das Ideal.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **Permanenter Welkepunkt** – das verbleibende Wasser haftet stärker an Bodenpartikeln, als Wurzeln ziehen können. Es ist immer noch Wasser da unten; die Pflanze kann es nur nicht bekommen.

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: Der nutzbare Bereich zwischen Feldkapazität und Welkepunkt ist das **pflanzenverfügbare Wasser**.

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: Sandiger Boden hat große Poren, die schnell ablaufen, und hält vielleicht einen Zoll davon pro Fuß Tiefe.

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: Schlammlehm hält zwei oder mehr.

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: Diese einzige Zahl erklärt, warum ein Sandhügel in Nebraska häufige, leichte Bewässerung benötigt, während ein Schlufflehm in Illinois eine Woche lang ausrollen kann.

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: Wenn das verfügbare Wasser zur Neige geht, gerät die Pflanze in **Wassermestress**.

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: Ihre erste Verteidigung ist das Schließen der Stomata – was den Wasserverlust stoppt, aber auch die CO2-Aufnahme stoppt, sodass das Wachstum pausiert.

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: Drückt man weiter, rollen sich die Blätter ein, verwelken und fallen ab.

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: Das Timing ist wichtiger als die Gesamtmenge: Stress während der Blüte und Bestäubung kostet weitaus mehr Ertrag als derselbe Stress während des frühen vegetativen Wachstums.

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: Bei Mais können ein paar trockene Tage beim Rispenschieben den Ertrag um ein Drittel senken.

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: Das gegenteilige Versagen ist genauso real.

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **Staunässe** füllt jede Pore, Wurzeln ersticken und in warmem Boden können sie in 48 bis 72 Stunden sterben.

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: Aus diesem Grund ist **Entwässerung** – Oberflächenplanie oder vergrabene perforierte Rohre namens **Dränage** – eine Form des Wassermanagements, die ebenso wichtig ist wie die Bewässerung.

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: Ein Großteil des amerikanischen Mittleren Westens ist nur deshalb landwirtschaftlich nutzbar, weil er dräniert wurde.

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: Wie liefern wir also Wasser?

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: Drei große Familien, in grober Reihenfolge der Effizienz:

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **Oberflächenbewässerung (Überschwemmung/Furche)** – Wasser läuft durch Schwerkraft das Feld hinunter. Billig, uralt, keine Energiekosten, aber typischerweise erreichen nur 40 bis 60 % des ausgebrachten Wassers die Wurzelzone. Der Rest läuft ab oder versickert an den Wurzeln vorbei.

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **Regnerbewässerung** – unter Druck, von oben gesprüht. Der Kreisberegner, diese grünen Kreise, die man aus einem Flugzeug über Kansas sieht, ist die vorherrschende Form. Etwa 70 bis 90 % effizient; Niederdruck-Abwurfdüsen in Bodennähe schlagen Hochdruckkanonen, weil weniger Spray im Flug verdunstet.

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **Tropfbewässerung / Mikro-Bewässerung** – Emitter geben langsam Wasser direkt an der Basis jeder Pflanze ab. 85 bis 95 % effizient, ermöglicht die Zufuhr von Dünger im Wasser (**Fertigation**) und hält das Laub trocken, was einige Krankheiten unterdrückt. Der Haken sind die Anschaffungskosten und verstopfte Emitter, wenn das Wasser nicht gefiltert wird.

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: Die Entscheidung, *wann* bewässert werden soll, folgt einer von zwei Logiken.

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **Bodenbasiert**: Sensoren in den Boden stecken und gießen, wenn die Feuchtigkeit einen Schwellenwert unterschreitet.

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **Wetterbasiert**: Ein Scheckbuch führen.

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: Schätzen, wie viel Wasser das Feld als **Evapotranspiration** (ET – Transpiration von Pflanzen plus Verdunstung aus dem Boden) verlassen hat, Regen abziehen und das Defizit auffüllen.

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: Einfach ausgedrückt:

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: Öffentliche ET-Netzwerke veröffentlichen täglich Zahlen genau zu diesem Zweck, und ein Kulturkoeffizient skaliert den Referenzwert auf das, was Sie in welchem Wachstumsstadium auch immer anbauen.

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: Eine weitere Idee, die man kennen sollte: **Defizitbewässerung**.

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: Manchmal spart ein gezieltes Unterbewässern während einer Phase, in der die Kultur unempfindlich ist, viel Wasser für einen geringen Ertragseinbruch – und bei Weintrauben verbessert leichter Stress tatsächlich die Fruchtqualität, indem er Zucker und Aromastoffe konzentriert.

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: Mehr Wasser ist nicht immer besser.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Im Alltag

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: Fliegen Sie an einem klaren Nachmittag nach Denver oder Wichita und blicken Sie nach unten.

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: Der Boden ist ein Quilt aus perfekten grünen Kreisen, von denen jeder etwa eine halbe Meile breit ist, eingepackt in quadratische Felder.

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: Das sind Kreisberegnungsanlagen – ein eine viertel Meile langer Regnerarm, der sich langsam um einen Brunnen dreht.

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: Die Ecken bleiben braun, weil der Arm sie nicht erreichen kann.

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: Die meisten dieser Brunnen zapfen den Ogallala-Aquifer an, die riesige Grundwasserschicht unter den High Plains.

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: Es ist eine nützliche Lektion in der Ökonomie der Bewässerung.

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: In Teilen des westlichen Kansas ist der Grundwasserspiegel seit Beginn des großflächigen Pumpens um mehr als 100 Fuß gesunken, und das Pumpen aus größerer Tiefe kostet jedes Jahr mehr Diesel oder Strom.

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: Dieser steigende Preis ist der Grund, warum Landwirte dort Hochdruckkanonen gegen Niederdruckdüsen austauschten, dann Bodenfeuchtesonden hinzufügten und in einigen Landkreisen freiwillig zustimmten, weniger zu pumpen.

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: Effizienz hörte auf, ein Umweltslogan zu sein, und wurde zu einem Posten auf der Rechnung.

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: Unterdessen im Central Valley in Kalifornien – das den Großteil der Mandeln, Pistazien und Verarbeitungstomaten in den USA anbaut.

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: – lief die Geschichte andersherum.

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: Permanente Baum- und Rebkulturen können in einem trockenen Jahr nicht wie eine einjährige Reihenkultur brachgelegt werden; man bewässert entweder den Obstgarten oder verliert eine 20-jährige Investition.

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: Dieser Druck trieb das Tal stark in Richtung Tropf- und Mikrobewässerung sowie zu vergrabenen Tropfschläuchen bei Tomaten.

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: Wasser in diesem System wird auf einem offenen Markt gehandelt, in einem Dürrejahr manchmal für mehrere hundert Dollar pro Acre-Foot, was jeden Prozentpunkt Effizienz zu echtem Geld macht.

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: Sie können dieselbe Physik in Ihrem eigenen Garten beobachten.

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: Gießen Sie einen Rasen um 14 Uhr.

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: im August und ein signifikanter Anteil verdunstet, bevor er landet.

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Gießen um 5 Uhr morgens.

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: und fast alles zieht ein – derselbe Schlauch, dieselben Minuten, mehr Wasser in der Wurzelzone.

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: Und der Standardrat, tief, aber seltener zu gießen, ist ebenfalls Bodenphysik: Ein leichtes tägliches Besprühen benässt nur den obersten Zoll, sodass die Wurzeln flach bleiben und die Pflanze in dem Moment fragil wird, in dem Sie einen Tag auslassen.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Zusammenfassung in drei Zeilen

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. Pflanzen müssen ihre Stomata öffnen, um CO2 aufzunehmen, daher ist Transpiration – der Verlust von Wasser an die Luft – ein unvermeidlicher Preis der Photosynthese, angetrieben durch die Trockenheit der Luft.

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. Nutzwasser im Boden liegt zwischen Feldkapazität und Welkepunkt; zu wenig verursacht Wassermestress, der während der Blüte am meisten schadet, und zu viel erstickt die Wurzeln, weshalb Entwässerung genauso wichtig ist wie Bewässerung.

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. Bewässerungsmethoden reichen von billigen, undichten Flutungsanlagen bis hin zu teuren, präzisen Tropfsystemen, und die Planung erfolgt entweder durch Bodenfeuchtesensoren oder ein Evapotranspirations-Scheckbuch, das Wasserzufluss gegen Wasserabfluss verfolgt.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ Selbsttest

segments.tr: - A) Etwa 50%

segments.tr: - C) Weniger als 1%

segments.src: - D) About 90%
segments.tr: - D) Etwa 90%

segments.tr: R/F: Boden bei „Feldkapazität“ ist der feuchteste mögliche Zustand, bei dem jeder Porenraum mit Wasser gefüllt ist.**

segments.src: Which irrigation method is generally the most efficient at delivering water to the root zone?**
segments.tr: Welche Bewässerungsmethode ist im Allgemeinen am effizientesten bei der Wasserzufuhr zur Wurzelzone?**

segments.src: - A) Furrow (surface) irrigation
segments.tr: - A) Furchen- (Oberflächen-) Bewässerung

segments.tr: - B) Hochdruck-Regnerkanonen

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **Transpiration** – Wasser, das durch die Stomata aus den Blättern einer Pflanze verdunstet; der unvermeidliche Preis des Öffnens von Poren zur CO2-Aufnahme.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **Stomata** – Einstellbare mikroskopische Poren auf Blattoberflächen, die CO2 hinein- und Wasserdampf herauslassen; die Pflanze schließt sie unter Stress.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **Feldkapazität** – Die Feuchtigkeit, die ein Boden hält, nachdem die Schwerkraft die großen Poren entleert hat, sodass sowohl Wasser als auch Luft für die Wurzeln verfügbar sind; der Zielzustand.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **Permanenter Welkepunkt** – Das Feuchtigkeitsniveau, bei dem das verbleibende Bodenwasser zu fest gehalten wird, als dass Wurzeln es extrahieren könnten, und sich die Pflanze nicht erholen kann.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** – Kombinierter Wasserverlust durch Pflanzentranspiration und Bodenoberflächenverdunstung; die „Entnahme“-Zahl bei der Bewässerungsplanung.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **Dränage** – Perforierte Rohre, die unterhalb der Wurzelzone vergraben sind, um überschüssiges Wasser abzuführen und zu verhindern, dass Wurzeln in gesättigtem Boden ersticken.

segments.src: *Answers: 1 — C.
segments.tr: *Antworten: 1 — C.

segments.src: Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: Weit über 99 % des aufgenommenen Wassers fließt durch und transpiriert weg; nur ein winziger Bruchteil endet als Pflanzengewebe.

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: Das ist der Handel, den eine Pflanze eingeht, um CO2 für die Photosynthese zu bekommen.

segments.src: 2 — X (False).
segments.tr: 2 — F (Falsch).

segments.src: The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: Der feuchteste Zustand ist die Sättigung, bei der jede Pore mit Wasser gefüllt ist und die Wurzeln keinen Sauerstoff haben.

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: Feldkapazität ist das, was nach dem Entleeren der großen Poren durch die Schwerkraft übrig bleibt, und es ist genau deshalb der wünschenswerte Zustand, weil sowohl Wasser als auch Luft vorhanden sind.

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: Tropf- und Mikrobewässerung liefern Wasser direkt an der Pflanzenbasis und erreichen typischerweise 85 bis 95 % Effizienz gegenüber etwa 40 bis 60 % bei Oberflächenmethoden.

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: Der Kompromiss sind hohe Installationskosten und die Notwendigkeit von sauberem, gefiltertem Wasser, um verstopfte Emitter zu vermeiden.*

vi.title: [Nông nghiệp 101 #5] Một Cây Ngô Uống Nước Như Một Vòi Chữa Cháy — Và Giữ Lại Gần Như Không Có Gì

segments.src: > Crops move enormous amounts of water from soil to air, and irrigation is really just the job of keeping that pipeline from running dry — without drowning the roots.
segments.tr: > Cây trồng di chuyển lượng nước khổng lồ từ đất lên không khí, và tưới tiêu thực sự chỉ là việc giữ cho đường ống đó không chảy hết nước — mà không làm chết chìm rễ.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Here's a fact that surprises most people: a plant uses less than 1% of the water it absorbs to actually build itself.
segments.tr: Đây là một sự thật làm ngạc nhiên hầu hết mọi người: một cây chỉ sử dụng ít hơn 1% nước mà nó hấp thụ để thực sự xây dựng chính nó.

segments.src: The other 99%-plus passes straight through and evaporates out of its leaves.
segments.tr: 99% còn lại đi thẳng qua và bay hơi ra khỏi lá của nó.

segments.src: That process is called **transpiration**, and it isn't waste.
segments.tr: Quá trình đó được gọi là **thoát hơi**, và nó không phải lãng phí.

segments.src: It's the price of eating.
segments.tr: Đó là giá của việc ăn.

segments.src: Leaves are covered in microscopic adjustable pores called **stomata**.
segments.tr: Lá được phủ bởi các lỗ nhỏ có thể điều chỉnh được gọi là **khí khổ**.

segments.src: A plant has to open them to let carbon dioxide in — CO2 is the raw material for photosynthesis, the sugar-making reaction that becomes grain, fruit, and fiber.
segments.tr: Một cây phải mở chúng để cho carbon dioxide vào — CO2 là nguyên liệu thô cho quang hợp, phản ứng tạo đường được chuyển thành hạt lúa, trái cây và chất xơ.

segments.src: But the inside of a leaf is a wet surface, and the air outside is usually drier.
segments.tr: Nhưng bên trong của một chiếc lá là một bề mặt ướt, và không khí bên ngoài thường khô hơn.

segments.src: The instant those pores open, water vapor rushes out.
segments.tr: Ngay khi những lỗ đó mở, hơi nước phóng thoát.

segments.src: There's no way to inhale CO2 without exhaling water.
segments.tr: Không có cách nào để hít CO2 mà không thở ra nước.

segments.src: Farmers sometimes call this the plant's "carbon-for-water trade."
segments.tr: Nông dân đôi khi gọi đây là "giao dịch carbon-nước" của cây.

segments.src: The escaping vapor pulls a continuous thread of water up from the roots.
segments.tr: Hơi thoát kéo một sợi nước liên tục từ rễ lên.

segments.src: Water molecules cling to each other (cohesion) and to the walls of the plant's narrow plumbing, the **xylem**.
segments.tr: Các phân tử nước bám vào nhau (sự dính kết) và vào các thành của hệ ống hẹp của cây, **gỗ lõi**.

segments.src: So evaporation at the top literally drags the column upward — no pump, no heart, just tension.
segments.tr: Vì vậy sự bay hơi ở trên kéo cột nước lên — không có bơm, không có tim, chỉ có lực căng.

segments.src: A tall corn plant on a hot July day in Iowa can move two to four liters through this straw.
segments.tr: Một cây ngô cao vào một ngày tháng Bảy nóng nực ở Iowa có thể di chuyển hai đến bốn lít qua ống này.

segments.src: The dryness of the air sets the pull rate.
segments.tr: Độ khô của không khí xác định tốc độ kéo.

segments.src: That's **vapor pressure deficit** (VPD) — the gap between how much moisture the air is holding and how much it could hold.
segments.tr: Đó là **thâm hụt áp suất hơi** (VPD) — khoảng cách giữa độ ẩm hiện tại của không khí và độ ẩm tối đa nó có thể chứa.

segments.src: Hot, dry, windy days mean a big deficit and a hard pull.
segments.tr: Những ngày nóng, khô, gió lớn có nghĩa là thâm hụt lớn và kéo mạnh.

segments.src: Cool, humid, still days mean a gentle one.
segments.tr: Những ngày mát, ẩm, tĩnh lặng có nghĩa là kéo nhẹ nhàng.

segments.src: This is why the same field can need double the water in a heat wave.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao cùng một cánh đồng có thể cần gấp đôi lượng nước trong một đợt nắng nóng.

segments.src: Now the soil side.
segments.tr: Bây giờ là phía đất.

segments.src: Water in soil isn't a full tank you draw down evenly.
segments.tr: Nước trong đất không phải một bồn chứa đầy mà bạn hút đều đặn.

segments.src: Three landmarks matter:
segments.tr: Ba điểm mốc quan trọng:

segments.src: - **Saturation** — every pore is full of water, and none is full of air. Roots need oxygen too, so this is a countdown clock, not a good state.
segments.tr: - **Bão hòa** — mỗi lỗ đều đầy nước, và không có lỗ nào đầy không khí. Rễ cũng cần oxygen, vì vậy đây là một đồng hồ đếm ngược, không phải là trạng thái tốt.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — gravity has drained the big pores (usually a day or two after a soaking rain), water remains in the small ones, and air is back. This is the ideal.
segments.tr: - **Dung lượng ruộng** — trọng lực đã thoát nước khỏi các lỗ lớn (thường là một hoặc hai ngày sau một cơn mưa tươm tất), nước vẫn nằm trong các lỗ nhỏ, và không khí trở lại. Đây là trang thái lý tưởng.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — the remaining water clings to soil particles more tightly than roots can pull. There's still water down there; the plant just can't get it.
segments.tr: - **Điểm héo dẫn vĩnh viễn** — nước còn lại bám chặt vào các hạt đất hơn rễ có thể kéo. Vẫn còn nước ở đó; cây chỉ không thể lấy được nó.

segments.src: The usable range between field capacity and wilting point is **plant-available water**.
segments.tr: Phạm vi có thể sử dụng được giữa dung lượng ruộng và điểm héo là **nước khả dụng của cây**.

segments.src: Sandy soil has big pores that drain fast and holds maybe an inch of it per foot of depth.
segments.tr: Đất cát có các lỗ lớn thoát nước nhanh và chỉ giữ lại khoảng một inch nước trên mỗi foot độ sâu.

segments.src: Silt loam holds two or more.
segments.tr: Đất thịt sét giữ lại hai inch hoặc hơn.

segments.src: That single number explains why a Nebraska sand hill needs frequent light irrigation while an Illinois silt loam can coast for a week.
segments.tr: Con số đơn lẻ đó giải thích tại sao một đồi cát Nebraska cần tưới nhẹ thường xuyên trong khi đất thịt sét Illinois có thể duy trì được một tuần.

segments.src: When available water runs low, the plant hits **water stress**.
segments.tr: Khi nước khả dụng giảm thấp, cây bị **stress hạn nước**.

segments.src: Its first defense is to close stomata — which stops water loss but also stops CO2 intake, so growth pauses.
segments.tr: Biện pháp phòng vệ đầu tiên của nó là đóng khí khổ — điều này ngăn chặn mất nước nhưng cũng ngăn chặn việc hấp thụ CO2, vì vậy sự phát triển tạm dừng.

segments.src: Push further and leaves roll, wilt, and drop.
segments.tr: Tiếp tục và lá cuộn, héo và rơi.

segments.src: Timing matters more than total: stress during flowering and pollination costs far more yield than the same stress during early vegetative growth.
segments.tr: Thời điểm quan trọng hơn tổng lượng: stress trong lúc ra hoa và thụ phấn mất năng suất nhiều hơn stress tương tự trong giai đoạn phát triển thực vật sớm.

segments.src: In corn, a few dry days at silking can cut yield by a third.
segments.tr: Ở lúa mì, một vài ngày khô vào lúc phát tơ có thể giảm năng suất xuống một phần ba.

segments.src: The opposite failure is just as real.
segments.tr: Sự thất bại ngược lại cũng thực tế như vậy.

segments.src: **Waterlogging** fills every pore, roots suffocate, and in warm soil they can die in 48 to 72 hours.
segments.tr: **Ngập nước** lấp đầy mỗi lỗ, rễ bị ngạt, và trong đất ấm chúng có thể chết trong 48 đến 72 giờ.

segments.src: This is why **drainage** — surface grading, or buried perforated pipe called **tile drainage** — is a form of water management every bit as important as irrigation.
segments.tr: Đây là lý do tại sao **thoát nước** — san phẳng bề mặt, hoặc ống có lỗ chôn dưới lòng đất được gọi là **thoát nước gạch** — là một hình thức quản lý nước quan trọng không kém tưới tiêu.

segments.src: Much of the American Midwest is farmable only because it was tiled.
segments.tr: Phần lớn Trung Tây Hoa Kỳ chỉ có thể canh tác được vì nó đã được lắp hệ thống thoát nước.

segments.src: So how do we deliver water?
segments.tr: Vậy chúng ta cung cấp nước như thế nào?

segments.src: Three broad families, in rough order of efficiency:
segments.tr: Ba họ rộng, theo thứ tự hiệu suất:

segments.src: - **Surface (flood/furrow) irrigation** — water runs down the field by gravity. Cheap, ancient, no energy cost, but typically only 40 to 60% of applied water reaches the root zone. The rest runs off or percolates past the roots.
segments.tr: - **Tưới tiêu bề mặt (ngập/máng)** — nước chảy xuống cánh đồng theo trọng lực. Rẻ tiền, cổ xưa, không có chi phí năng lượng, nhưng thường chỉ 40 đến 60% nước được cung cấp mới tiếp cận vùng rễ. Phần còn lại chảy trôi hoặc thẩm thấu quá rễ.

segments.src: - **Sprinkler irrigation** — pressurized, sprayed from above. The center pivot, those green circles you see from an airplane over Kansas, is the dominant form. Roughly 70 to 90% efficient; low-pressure drop nozzles near the ground beat high-pressure guns because less spray evaporates in flight.
segments.tr: - **Tưới tiêu bằng phun sương** — áp lực, phun từ trên cao. Trục quay tâm, những vòng tròn xanh bạn thấy từ máy bay trên Kansas, là dạng phổ biến nhất. Hiệu suất khoảng 70 đến 90%; những đầu phun áp lực thấp gần mặt đất tốt hơn những khẩu súng áp lực cao vì ít phun bay hơi trong chuyến bay.

segments.src: - **Drip / micro-irrigation** — emitters release water slowly right at the base of each plant. 85 to 95% efficient, allows fertilizer to be delivered in the water (**fertigation**), and keeps foliage dry, which suppresses some diseases. The catch is upfront cost and clogged emitters if the water isn't filtered.
segments.tr: - **Tưới giọt / tưới vi mô** — các thiết bị phát thải nước từ từ ngay ở gốc mỗi cây. Hiệu suất 85 đến 95%, cho phép phân bón được vận chuyển trong nước (**tưới phân**), và giữ lá khô, điều này ngăn chặn một số bệnh. Điểm yếu là chi phí ban đầu và các thiết bị phát thải bị tắc nếu nước không được lọc.

segments.src: Deciding *when* to irrigate uses one of two logics.
segments.tr: Quyết định *khi nào* tưới tiêu sử dụng một trong hai logic.

segments.src: **Soil-based**: put sensors in the ground and water when moisture drops past a threshold.
segments.tr: **Dựa trên đất**: đặt cảm biến trong lòng đất và tưới khi độ ẩm giảm dưới ngưỡng.

segments.src: **Weather-based**: run a checkbook.
segments.tr: **Dựa trên thời tiết**: chạy một sổ cân đối.

segments.src: Estimate how much water left the field as **evapotranspiration** (ET — transpiration from plants plus evaporation from soil), subtract rain, and refill the deficit.
segments.tr: Ước tính lượng nước ra khỏi ruộng dưới dạng **thoát hơi nước** (ET — thoát hơi từ cây cộng với sự bay hơi từ đất), trừ lượng mưa, và bù lại mức thâm hụt.

segments.src: In plain terms:
segments.tr: Nói một cách đơn giản:

segments.src: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff
segments.tr: soil water today = soil water yesterday + rain + irrigation - ET - drainage - runoff

segments.src: Public ET networks publish daily numbers for exactly this purpose, and a crop coefficient scales the reference figure to whatever you're growing at whatever growth stage.
segments.tr: Các mạng ET công cộng xuất bản các số liệu hàng ngày cho mục đích chính xác này, và một hệ số cây trồng mở rộng con số tham chiếu cho bất kỳ loại cây nào bạn trồng ở bất kỳ giai đoạn phát triển nào.

segments.src: One more idea worth knowing: **deficit irrigation**.
segments.tr: Một ý tưởng khác đáng biết: **tưới tiêu thâm hụt**.

segments.src: Sometimes deliberately under-watering during a stage where the crop is insensitive saves a lot of water for a small yield hit — and in wine grapes, mild stress actually improves fruit quality by concentrating sugars and flavor compounds.
segments.tr: Đôi khi cố tình ít tưới nước trong giai đoạn khi cây trồng không nhạy cảm sẽ tiết kiệm rất nhiều nước để lấy một mất năng suất nhỏ — và ở nho rượu, stress nhẹ thực sự cải thiện chất lượng trái cây bằng cách tập trung đường và hợp chất hương vị.

segments.src: More water is not always better.
segments.tr: Nhiều nước không phải lúc nào cũng tốt hơn.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Fly into Denver or Wichita on a clear afternoon and look down.
segments.tr: Bay vào Denver hoặc Wichita vào một buổi chiều quang đãng và nhìn xuống.

segments.src: The ground is a quilt of perfect green circles, each about half a mile across, packed inside square fields.
segments.tr: Mặt đất là một bảng vá những vòng tròn xanh hoàn hảo, mỗi cái khoảng nửa dặm ngang, được xếp bên trong các cánh đồng hình vuông.

segments.src: Those are center pivots — a quarter-mile arm of sprinklers slowly rotating around a well.
segments.tr: Đó là các trục quay tâm — một cánh tay tưới nước dài một phần tư dặm chậm chạp quay xung quanh một giếng.

segments.src: The corners stay brown because the arm can't reach them.
segments.tr: Các góc vẫn nâu vì cánh tay không thể tiếp cận chúng.

segments.src: Most of those wells tap the Ogallala Aquifer, the vast groundwater layer under the High Plains.
segments.tr: Hầu hết những giếng đó khai thác Tầng chứa nước Ogallala, lớp nước ngầm rộng lớn dưới High Plains.

segments.src: It's a useful lesson in the economics of irrigation.
segments.tr: Đó là một bài học hữu ích về kinh tế của tưới tiêu.

segments.src: In parts of western Kansas the water table has dropped by more than 100 feet since large-scale pumping began, and pumping from deeper costs more diesel or electricity every year.
segments.tr: Ở một số nơi ở Kansas phía tây, mực nước ngầm đã giảm hơn 100 feet kể từ khi bắt đầu bơm quy mô lớn, và bơm từ sâu hơn tốn nhiều diesel hoặc điện mỗi năm.

segments.src: That rising cost is why farmers there swapped high-pressure guns for low-drop nozzles, then added soil moisture probes, and in some counties voluntarily agreed to pump less.
segments.tr: Chi phí tăng đó là lý do tại sao những nông dân ở đó đổi những khẩu súng áp lực cao lấy những đầu phun áp lực thấp, sau đó thêm những cảm biến độ ẩm đất, và ở một số quận tự nguyện đồng ý bơm ít hơn.

segments.src: Efficiency stopped being an environmental slogan and became a line item.
segments.tr: Hiệu suất ngừng là một khẩu hiệu môi trường và trở thành một mục.

segments.src: Meanwhile in California's Central Valley — which grows most of the almonds, pistachios, and processing tomatoes in the U.S.
segments.tr: Trong khi đó ở Thung lũng Trung tâm California — nơi trồng hầu hết hạnh nhân, hạt dẻ và cà chua chế biến ở Hoa Kỳ

segments.src: — the story went the other way.
segments.tr: — câu chuyện đã đi theo hướng khác.

segments.src: Permanent tree and vine crops can't be fallowed in a dry year the way an annual row crop can; you either water the orchard or lose a 20-year investment.
segments.tr: Cây lâu năm và cây nho không thể để hoang trong năm khô hạn như cách một cây trồng hàng năm có thể; bạn hoặc tưới vườn cây hoặc mất một khoản đầu tư 20 năm.

segments.src: That pressure pushed the valley heavily toward drip and micro-sprinklers, and toward buried drip lines in tomatoes.
segments.tr: Áp lực đó đã đẩy thung lũng nặng nề hướng tới tưới giọt và các vòi phun vi mô, và hướng tới các ống tưới giọt chôn dưới lòng đất trong cà chua.

segments.src: Water in that system trades on an open market, sometimes for several hundred dollars an acre-foot in a drought year, which makes every percentage point of efficiency worth real money.
segments.tr: Nước trong hệ thống đó giao dịch trên một thị trường mở, đôi khi với giá vài trăm đô la mỗi acre-foot trong năm hạn hán, điều này làm cho mỗi điểm phần trăm của hiệu suất có giá trị thực tế.

segments.src: You can watch the same physics in your own yard.
segments.tr: Bạn có thể xem cùng một vật lý trong sân của riêng bạn.

segments.src: Water a lawn at 2 p.m.
segments.tr: Tưới cỏ lúc 2 giờ chiều

segments.src: in August and a meaningful share evaporates before it lands.
segments.tr: vào tháng Tám và một phần có ý nghĩa bay hơi trước khi nó tiếp đất.

segments.src: Water at 5 a.m.
segments.tr: Tưới lúc 5 giờ sáng

segments.src: and nearly all of it soaks in — same hose, same minutes, more water in the root zone.
segments.tr: và gần như toàn bộ nó thấm vào — cùng một vòi, cùng thời gian, nhiều nước hơn trong vùng rễ.

segments.src: And the standard advice to water deeply but less often is soil physics too: a light daily sprinkle wets only the top inch, so roots stay shallow and the plant becomes fragile the moment you skip a day.
segments.tr: Và lời khuyên tiêu chuẩn tưới sâu nhưng ít thường xuyên cũng là vật lý đất: một chút phun sương hàng ngày chỉ làm ướt một inch trên cùng, vì vậy rễ ở nông và cây trở nên mỏng manh ngay khi bạn bỏ qua một ngày.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Summary
segments.tr: ## Tóm Tắt Ba Dòng

segments.src: 1. Plants must open their stomata to take in CO2, so transpiration — losing water to the air — is an unavoidable cost of photosynthesis, driven by how dry the air is.
segments.tr: 1. Cây phải mở khí khổ của chúng để hấp thụ CO2, vì vậy thoát hơi — mất nước vào không khí — là một chi phí không thể tránh khỏi của quang hợp, được thúc đẩy bởi độ khô của không khí.

segments.src: 2. Usable soil water sits between field capacity and the wilting point; too little causes water stress that hurts most during flowering, and too much suffocates roots, which is why drainage matters as much as irrigation.
segments.tr: 2. Nước đất có thể sử dụng được nằm giữa dung lượng ruộng và điểm héo; quá ít gây ra stress hạn nước làm tổn thương nhất trong lúc ra hoa, và quá nhiều ngạt rễ, đây là lý do tại sao thoát nước quan trọng không kém tưới tiêu.

segments.src: 3. Irrigation methods run from cheap, leaky flood systems to expensive, precise drip, and scheduling is done either by soil moisture sensors or by an evapotranspiration checkbook that tracks water in versus water out.
segments.tr: 3. Các phương pháp tưới tiêu từ hệ thống ngập rẻ tiền, rò rỉ đến tưới giọt đắt tiền, chính xác, và lập lịch được thực hiện bằng cảm biến độ ẩm đất hoặc bằng một sổ cân đối thoát hơi nước theo dõi nước vào và nước ra.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Thuật Ngữ Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Transpiration** — Water evaporating out of a plant's leaves through the stomata; the unavoidable cost of opening pores to absorb CO2.
segments.tr: - **Thoát hơi** — Nước bay hơi ra khỏi lá của cây thông qua khí khổ; chi phí không thể tránh khỏi của việc mở lỗ để hấp thụ CO2.

segments.src: - **Stomata** — Adjustable microscopic pores on leaf surfaces that let CO2 in and water vapor out; the plant closes them under stress.
segments.tr: - **Khí khổ** — Những lỗ nhỏ có thể điều chỉnh được trên bề mặt lá cho phép CO2 vào và hơi nước ra; cây đóng chúng dưới sức ép.

segments.src: - **Field capacity** — The moisture a soil holds after gravity has drained the large pores, leaving both water and air available to roots; the target condition.
segments.tr: - **Dung lượng ruộng** — Độ ẩm mà đất giữ lại sau khi trọng lực đã thoát nước khỏi các lỗ lớn, để lại cả nước và không khí cho rễ; trạng thái mục tiêu.

segments.src: - **Permanent wilting point** — The moisture level at which remaining soil water is held too tightly for roots to extract, and the plant cannot recover.
segments.tr: - **Điểm héo dẫn vĩnh viễn** — Mức độ ẩm mà nước đất còn lại bám chặt vào không thể được rễ kéo ra, và cây không thể phục hồi.

segments.src: - **Evapotranspiration (ET)** — Combined water loss from plant transpiration and soil surface evaporation; the "withdrawal" figure in irrigation scheduling.
segments.tr: - **Thoát hơi nước (ET)** — Mất nước kết hợp từ thoát hơi của cây và sự bay hơi của bề mặt đất; con số "rút tiền" trong lập lịch tưới tiêu.

segments.src: - **Tile drainage** — Perforated pipe buried below the root zone to carry away excess water and prevent roots from suffocating in saturated soil.
segments.tr: - **Thoát nước gạch** — Ống có lỗ chôn dưới vùng rễ để xả nước thừa và ngăn chặn rễ bị ngạt trong đất bão hòa.

segments.src: Well over 99% of absorbed water passes through and transpires away; only a tiny fraction ends up as plant tissue.
segments.tr: Hơn 99% nước được hấp thụ đi qua và thoát hơi; chỉ một phần rất nhỏ kết thúc dưới dạng mô cây.

segments.src: That's the trade a plant makes to get CO2 for photosynthesis.
segments.tr: Đó là giao dịch mà một cây thực hiện để lấy CO2 cho quang hợp.

segments.src: The wettest state is saturation, where every pore is water-filled and roots have no oxygen.
segments.tr: Trạng thái ướt nhất là bão hòa, nơi mỗi lỗ đầy nước và rễ không có oxygen.

segments.src: Field capacity is what remains after gravity drains the large pores, and it's the desirable condition precisely because water and air are both present.
segments.tr: Dung lượng ruộng là những gì còn lại sau khi trọng lực thoát nước khỏi các lỗ lớn, và đó là tình trạng mong muốn chính xác vì cả nước và không khí đều hiện diện.

segments.src: Drip and micro-irrigation deliver water directly at the plant base and typically reach 85 to 95% efficiency, versus roughly 40 to 60% for surface methods.
segments.tr: Tưới giọt và tưới vi mô cung cấp nước trực tiếp tại gốc cây và thường đạt hiệu suất 85 đến 95%, so với khoảng 40 đến 60% cho các phương pháp bề mặt.

segments.src: The trade-off is high installation cost and the need for clean, filtered water to avoid clogged emitters.*
segments.tr: Sự đánh đổi là chi phí cài đặt cao và nhu cầu nước sạch, được lọc để tránh các thiết bị phát thải bị tắc.*
